body_text:
2026 멕시코 정부초청 장학생 선발을 아래와 같이 안내드리니, 관심있는 학생들의 많은 지원 바랍니다.

1. 선발과정: 학·석사 교환과정, 석사 학위과정, 박사(후) 연구과정

나. 지원 마감일: ~ 2026.6.22.(월) 3:00 p.m. *멕시코 중부시간 기준

다. 제출서류 등 세부 사항: <붙임> 파일 참조

MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS
MEXICAN AGENCY FOR INTERNATIONAL DEVELOPMENT COOPERATION
AMEXCID

1) OBJECTIVE
To contribute to the development of highly qualified human capital by granting scholarships
for full-time, in-person academic programs.

2) SCHOLARSHIP TYPES
Types Maximum duration
Undergraduate Mobility Up to 12 months
Master’s Mobility Up to 12 months
Master’s Degree Up to 24 months

Types Minimum and Maximum Duration
Doctoral Research Fellowship 6 to 12 Months
Postdoctoral Research Fellowship 6 to 12 Months

3) SCHOLARSHIP BENEFITS

AMEXCID will grant selected candidates:

1. For Master’s, Undergraduate Mobility and Master’s Mobility: a monthly stipend equivalent
to four (4) times the monthly value of the Unit of Measurement and Update (UMA), currently
$14,264.88 MXN. Paid monthly in arrears; subject to legal changes. The maintenance
payment is made at the end of the month, in accordance with what AMEXCID indicates.
2. For doctoral and postdoctoral research fellowships, the monthly living allowance is 5 (five)
times the monthly value of the Measurement and Update Unit (UMA), currently equivalent
to $17,831.10 (seventeen thousand eight hundred thirty-one pesos 10/100 M.N.). The
Measurement and Update Unit (UMA) is subject to changes established by law. The living
allowance is paid in arrears. The maintenance payment is made at the end of the month, in
accordance with what AMEXCID indicates.

2

Avenida Juárez No. 20, Plaza Juárez, Col. Centro, CP 06010, Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de México. Tel:
(55) 3686 5100 ext.5275 www.gob.mx/sre
3. Enrollment and tuition fees, in accordance with the provisions of each Mexican educational
institution’s program (Appendix 1), and subject to the final decision of each institution, as
stated in the acceptance letter issued to each applicant.
4. Health insurance through the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS). Coverage will begin
in the seventh month of the fellowship and will last for a period similar to the duration of
the fellowship. (Appendix 2).
5. Exemption from Mexican visa issuance fees.
6. International airfare upon successful completion of the scholarship. The ticket will be
provided in economy class and according to the flight route deemed most convenient by
AMEXCID. Please refer to the list of countries eligible for this benefit (Appendix 3).
7. Domestic Transportation. (Foreign bus) If studies are conducted outside Mexico City,
transportation costs will be covered from Mexico City to the host city of the receiving
academic institution, and back to Mexico City upon completion of the scholarship period,
provided that the student has successfully completed all academic requirements. This
applies only to either domestic airfare or ground transportation. (Appendix 4).

Important Notes
1. In all applicable cases, AMEXCID will purchase the airline ticket; any tickets purchased
individually will not be eligible for reimbursement.
2. Any changes the scholarship recipient wishes to make to the airline ticket purchased by
AMEXCID after it has been issued will be the recipient’s responsibility.
3. If the applicable domestic transportation is by land, the scholar must pay for the bus ticket
and will be reimbursed for the amount spent.
4. The administration and management of the aforementioned benefits will be the
responsibility of AMEXCID’s Scholarship office, and selected candidates will be notified of
these details before the scholarship is formalized.

4) APPLICATION SCHEDULE
ACTIVITY DATES
Call for applications May 21, 2026
Application registration in SIGCA (Academic
Cooperation Management System):
https://sigca.sre.gob.mx /
May 21 – June 22, 2026
Notification of results to selected candidates Between 6 and 10 Jul 2026

Scholarships will begin between August and before November 10, 2026, with a minimum
duration of 6 months.

3

Avenida Juárez No. 20, Plaza Juárez, Col. Centro, CP 06010, Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de México. Tel:
(55) 3686 5100 ext.5275 www.gob.mx/sre
5) APPLICATION
Applications must comply with the provisions of this Call for Applications, including the
documents referred to therein and the corresponding forms, in accordance with the following
terms:

1. Applications will be accepted in electronic format through the Academic Cooperation
Management System (SIGCA) (https://sigca.sre.gob.mx) during the application period.
2. Applications must be submitted in Spanish.
3. The SIGCA portal will remain open to receive applications from 6:00 p.m. on May 21, 2026,
until 3:00 p.m. on June 22, 2026, Central Mexico Time.
4. Only one application per person will be accepted; in the event of duplication, the application
will be automatically disqualified.'
5. Individuals with more than one nationality must submit a single application, which must
correspond to one of the eligible countries listed in this Call for Applications (Annex 5). The
application must be submitted according to the nationality with which the individual will be
accredited.
6. Applications from the institutions stipulated in Annex 1 and section 2 of this Call for
Applications will be accepted.

6) ARE INELIGIBLE
1. Foreign diplomats accredited in Mexico, as well as their immediate family members.
2. Foreign nationals residing in Mexico who do not hold a Temporary Resident Student Card
issued by the Mexican government.
3. Foreign nationals who also hold Mexican nationality, including children of Mexican parents.
4. Foreign nationals who hold a Mexican family reunification visa or who aspire to obtain one.
5. Applicants who received a scholarship in the immediately preceding year from any Federal
Government institution.
6. Those who hold a scholarship awarded by any Mexican government agency.
7. Former AMEXCID scholarship recipients applying for a scholarship, provided that the same
number of months have not yet passed since they received the scholarship. 8. Former
scholarship recipients who did not successfully complete the scholarship awarded by
AMEXCID in previous calls for applications.
9. Individuals under 18 years of age at the time of application.

4

Avenida Juárez No. 20, Plaza Juárez, Col. Centro, CP 06010, Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de México. Tel:
(55) 3686 5100 ext.5275 www.gob.mx/sre
10. Applicants residing in a country other than their country of nationality, or those with the
support, recommendation, or sponsorship of institutions located outside their country of
origin.

AMEXCID may verify the accuracy of the information provided by scholarship applicants at
any time and will take appropriate action in accordance with applicable regulations if false
information is provided.

7) DOCUMENT REQUIREMENTS.
1. Documents written in a language other than Spanish must be accompanied by a simple
translation into Spanish on a separate sheet of paper and must be signed by the applicant.
2. AMEXCID staff will not make any changes to data or files in SIGCA, nor will they receive
physical files or files outside the system.
3. Applicants must submit their documents in color PDF format (maximum size: 1.8 MB).
4. All documents requested in this section must be attached to your application in the System
before the application deadline.
5. Documents must be legible.
6. On documents requiring a signature, the signature must match the one in your passport,
and you must sign in blue ink.

8) REQUIREMENTS:
Please attach all academic documents relevant to the type of study or research you will be
conducting, in addition to:
1. A copy of the applicant’s valid passport showing their identification information.
(Update your passport if it was issued before you turned 18)

2. A declaration letter typed on a word processor and signed by the applicant (Form 1).
3. A resume typed (CV) in a word processor. Maximum 4 pages, signed by the applicant (Form
2).
4. Copy of the medical certificate: Issued by a public or private healthcare institution no more
than 3 (three) months prior to the submission of the application, stating that the applicant
is in good health. (If the certificate is in a language other than Spanish, it must be
accompanied by a certified translation.)
5. If your native language is different from Spanish, you must present a B2 certificate or
higher in the Common European Framework of Reference (MCER)

5

Avenida Juárez No. 20, Plaza Juárez, Col. Centro, CP 06010, Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de México. Tel:
(55) 3686 5100 ext.5275 www.gob.mx/sre
Undergraduate exchange programs and graduate exchange programs:

1. A copy of the acceptance letter from the host university, issued no more than 60 calendar
days prior, indicating that the applicant has a grade point average of 85 (on a scale of 0 to
100 or 8.5 on a scale of 10), equivalent to the Mexican educational system, and specifying
the start and end dates of the program.
2. A copy of the letter issued by the home institution in which they agree to recognize/transfer
the academic credits for the courses or programs to be taken in Mexico.
3. If the exchange program is conducted in a language other than Spanish and different from
your native language, you must submit a copy of the letter issued by the host institution in
which it agrees to provide academic advising in another language, specifying the language
and the name of the advisor.
4. For exchange programs at the master’s level, you must submit a copy of bachelor’s degree.
5. Grades for the last period completed, issued by the institution of origin

Master’s Degree:

1. A letter of acceptance from the host university issued no more than 60 calendar days prior,
stating that the applicant has a grade point average of 85 (on a scale of 0 to 100) or 8.5 (on
a scale of 10), equivalent to the Mexican educational system, and specifying the start and
end dates of the program.
2. Copy of bachelor’s degree.
3. A copy of the academic transcript for the most recent semester, issued by the home
institution, which must show a minimum grade point average of 85 (on a scale of 0 to 100)
or 8.5 (on a scale of 10).
4. If the courses are taught in a language other than Spanish and different from your native
language, you must submit a copy of the letter issued by the host institution in which it
agrees to provide tutoring in another language, specifying the language and the name of
the tutor.

Research fellowships at the doctoral and postdoctoral levels:

1. Copy of the doctoral degree
2. A copy of the letter of acceptance from the institution where the research will be conducted.
The letter of acceptance must state that supervision will be provided for the research, as
well as the name of the person who will supervise the applicant and the title of the research
project.

6

Avenida Juárez No. 20, Plaza Juárez, Col. Centro, CP 06010, Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de México. Tel:
(55) 3686 5100 ext.5275 www.gob.mx/sre
3. If your research stay will be conducted in a language other than Spanish and different from
your native language, please provide a copy of the letter issued by the host institution in
which it commits to providing mentorship in another language, specifying the language
and the name of the mentor.
4. Letter of nomination from an academic or governmental institution, according to your
nationality, indicating the research to be carried out and the justification for the
nomination.
5. Project Description Letter (Form 3).

9) REQUIREMENTS FOR THE LETTER OF ACCEPTANCE OR INTRODUCTION
1. Display the institution's letterhead.
2. It must include the name and signature of the issuing authority (Director of the Office of
International Affairs, Director of Academic Exchange, Head of Graduate Studies, Graduate
Coordinator, etc.).
3. Indicate the duration of the studies or research, including start and end dates (in the
required format: DD/MM/YYYY).
4. Specify the type of studies to be undertaken (mobility at the undergraduate and master's
levels, master's research stay at the postgraduate level, specifying whether it is a doctoral
research stay or a postdoctoral stay).
5. Name of the academic program for training scholarships.
6. Full name of the research project to be conducted (Only for research stays).
7. Name of the campus and state where the studies or research stay will take place.

10) SELECTION CRITERIA
The selection of scholarship recipients is conducted without any distinction based on ethnic
origin, gender, age, disability, social status, health condition, religion, sexual orientation,
marital status, or any other circumstance or condition that violates human dignity and is
intended to nullify or undermine the rights and freedoms of individuals, and will be subject to
the following criteria:

1. Submission of all documents requested in this Call for Applications.
2. Distribution of scholarships by country.
3. The applicant’s record of academic excellence.
4. Preference will be given to applicants who have never received a scholarship from
AMEXCID.

7

Avenida Juárez No. 20, Plaza Juárez, Col. Centro, CP 06010, Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de México. Tel:
(55) 3686 5100 ext.5275 www.gob.mx/sre
5. In the order in which the application was submitted. (Preference will be given to
applications submitted first).
6. Distribution of scholarships by receiving institution in Mexico.

For further research, the following will be evaluated:
• Awards and honors, specialized supplementary training, and professional experience
related to each candidate’s academic or scientific field.
• Teaching experience, considering the number of years of service and whether the position
is full-time or part-time at the university or institution of higher education.
• At least one year of experience in leadership roles in university administration or public
research institutions, as well as other leadership positions.
Preference will be given to research on topics such as:

a) Sustainable food systems, child nutrition, access to nutritious food, and reducing food loss
and waste.
b) Research on eliminating discrimination and violence against women and girls, and
promoting their equal participation in decision-making and access to economic resources.
c) Studies on sustainable water management, access to safe drinking water and sanitation,
and the impact of climate change on water availability.
d) Research on renewable energy sources, energy efficiency, access to clean energy for all,
and emissions reduction.
e) Studies on social, economic, and political inequalities, including poverty reduction, the
promotion of social inclusion, and the protection of human rights.
f) Studies on sustainable consumption patterns, efficient resource management, waste
reduction, and the promotion of sustainable supply chains.
g) Research on climate change mitigation and adaptation, renewable energy, climate risk
management, and ecosystem protection.
h) Research on the protection, restoration, and sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems,
desertification, biodiversity, and sustainable forest management.

11) RESULTS
1. In accordance with the schedule for this call for applications, the decision regarding the
award of the scholarship will be communicated via email only to those selected by
AMEXCID. If you do not receive a notification, your application was not selected.
2. If AMEXCID does not receive confirmation of acceptance of the scholarship from the
selected candidate, AMEXCID may award the scholarship to another candidate who meets
the required criteria.
3. Admission to any of the higher education institutions participating in this call for
applications does not guarantee that the Mexican government will award a scholarship.

8

Avenida Juárez No. 20, Plaza Juárez, Col. Centro, CP 06010, Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de México. Tel:
(55) 3686 5100 ext.5275 www.gob.mx/sre
4. The final decision on the awarding of scholarships rests solely with the Government of
Mexico.
5. All decisions made during the selection process are final; therefore, no response will be
provided regarding rejected applications.
6. By registering on the platform (SIGCA), the applicant agrees to the terms and conditions of
this Call for Applications, as well as to the processing of personal data in accordance with
the General Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Obligated Entities and the
Federal Law on Transparency and Access to Public Information.

12) CONSIDERATIONS
1. No scholarships are awarded for the preparation of thesis work toward the completion of
an academic degree.
2. The scholarship is non-transferable and cannot be deferred to academic years beyond the
period for which it was awarded.
3. Once the scholarship has been awarded, the deadlines specified in the announcement of
the results will not be modified or extended, nor will there be any changes to the academic
program, institution, and/or research project.
4. Any expenses not specified in this Call for Proposals will not be covered or reimbursed by
AMEXCID.
5. Applications from individuals who, at the time of application, are studying, residing, or
being nominated from a country other than their country of nationality, or those who have
the support, recommendation, or sponsorship of institutions located outside their country
of origin, will not be considered.
6. The selected candidate will receive instructions via email on how to begin the process of
formalizing the award of the scholarship. If AMEXCID does not receive a response to its
communications within the specified timeframe, this may result in the cancellation of the
scholarship award and the selection of another candidate.
7. The selected candidate must submit their acceptance of the scholarship to AMEXCID in
order to facilitate the administrative procedures and to be bound by the terms and
conditions of this Call for Applications.
8. If the selected individual does not use the international air transportation service provided
by AMEXCID, they may request reimbursement for the expenses incurred.
9. By accepting the scholarship, the selected candidate agrees to comply with the “Rules
Applicable to Foreign Scholarship Recipients” (NABE’S), as well as any updates to these rules
during the scholarship period.

9

Avenida Juárez No. 20, Plaza Juárez, Col. Centro, CP 06010, Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de México. Tel:
(55) 3686 5100 ext.5275 www.gob.mx/sre
10. Any selected individual who stays for 180 days or longer, regardless of nationality, must
obtain the visa specified by the Office of Academic Exchange from the Mexican Embassy or
Consulate abroad.
11. The selected candidate must report to the offices of the Directorate of Academic Exchange
(DIA), located within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs—Mexican Agency for International
Development Cooperation, at the following address: Plaza Juárez No. 20, Planta baja, Col.
Centro, C.P. 06010, Mexico City, during business hours from 9:00 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. on
business days, within the first 10 (ten) calendar days of the first month of their scholarship.
The staff of the Scholarship office will inform them of the date on which they must attend.
12. The selected candidate will be considered a scholarship recipient provided that they submit
the required documentation to the Scholarship office and will be subject to the terms and
conditions of this call for applications.
13. The scholarship recipient must begin their studies or research between August and
November 10, 2026; otherwise, the scholarship will be revoked.
The scholarship recipient must cover their own medical expenses if necessary; therefore,
we recommend purchasing international health insurance that covers the period during
which they will not have access to medical care.

It is recommended that you have sufficient funds to cover your expenses for at least the first 60
days of your fellowship period.
